(By Sri. Ashok Kumar , Advocate)
 JUDGMENT

On 05.09.2023 Manchaiah , S/o. Motaiah, asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation from the respondents, who are the insurer and owner of motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JD-2490, alleging that on 18.08.2023 at 10.30 a.m. when crossing the Dr. Puneeth Raj Kumar road, Banashankari 3rd stage, rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JD-2490 drove the same negligently on the wrong lane, dashed the same to the back of Manchaiah , thereby caused the accident, caused grievous injuries to Manchaiah.
2. Manchaiah took treatment at Maharaja Agrasena hospital , Bengaluru 3.
As on the date of accident petitioner Manchaiah being aged about 85 years used to earn Rs.30,000/p.m. by vending milk and by doing agriculture.
4. Regarding accident Banashankari Traffic police registered crime No.442/2023 .

5. In response to the notice, respondents No.1 and 2 appeared through their respective Advocates,
filed separate written statements denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of the accident ,
nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner Manchaiah.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 27.02.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, on 18.08.2023 at about 10.30 a.m. on Dr.Punith Rajkumar Ring Road, opposite Apollo National Public School, BSK 3rd stage, Bengaluru, he met with an accident and sustained injuries, was due to actionable negligence act on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Manchaiah vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85129373/
2 registration No.KA-02-JD-2490 as alleged?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation ? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order ?
7. During the pendency of the petition, on 05.04.2024 petitioner Manchaiah expired.
8. On 29.08.2024 children of Manchaiah filed I.A.No.1 to 3 seeking permission to implead them as LRs of Manchaiah and continue the litigation.

After hearing the submission made on behalf of both the parties, this authority allowed I.A.No.1 to 3 , thereby permitted children of Manchaiah to get implead as LRs, then children of Manchaiah get impleaded as petitioners No.1(a) to 1(c).
9. On 05.03.2025, respondent No1 insurance company filed written statement to the amended petition.
10. After the death of Manchaiah and after filing of written statement by insurance company on 29.08.2024 this authority framed following additional issue.
Whether LRs of the original petitioner proves that in consequences of the injuries suffered in the accident dated 18.08.2023, on 05.04.2024 original petitioner Manchaiah expired?

11. On 05.03.2025 petitioner No.1(a) deposed as PW1 and produced 26 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.26.
12.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of petitioners and respondent No.1 and perused the records.

13. On the basis of material on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ...
In the Affirmative, Addl. Issue ...
In the Negative , Issue No.2 ...

Petitioners are entitle to receive Rs.9,12,267/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from 05.04.2024 from the respondents as compensation .
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 14. Issue No.1 and Addl. Issue: In the evidence PW1 Shivaramu stated that on 18.08.2023 at 10.30 a.m. when his father Manchaiah was crossing the Dr. Puneeth Raj Kumar Ring road towards Apollo National Public School, Banashankari 3rd stage, rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA- 02-JD-2490 drove the same negligently on the wrong lane, dashed the same to the back of Manchaiah , thereby caused the accident, caused grievous injuries to Manchaiah.

PW1 stated that immediately after the accident Manchaiah was shifted to Maharaja Agrasena hospital , Bengaluru , wherein first Manchaiah vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85129373/
3 aid/treatment has been provided from 18.08.2023 to 02.09.2023 , then shifted to Dwitiya Life Care hospital, Bengaluru , wherein treated as an inpatient from 02.09.2023 to 13.10.2023 and from 15.10.2023 to 23.03.2024 by spending Rs.25,00,000/-.

sentences.text: PW1 stated that inspite of better treatment on 05.04.2024 his father Manchaiah expired.
15. In the written statement respondents No.1 and 2 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.
16. In the cross-examination, PW1 submitted that he never witnessed the accident.
PW1 denied the suggestion that motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JD-2490 never dashed to Manchaiah.
PW1 submitted that in the residence his father Manchaiah expired and body of his father Manchaih was not subjected to autopsy.
PW1 submitted that as on the date of death of his father was aged about 84 years and denied the suggestion that due to age factor his father expired.

17. Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR pertaining to crime No.442/2023 registered by Banashankari Traffic police against rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JD-2490 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,338 of IPC section 134 (a & b), 187 of IMV Act on the basis of the statement of Manchaiah, S/p. Motaiah recorded on 18.08.2023 at 10.30 a.m. at Maharaja Agrasena hospital , Bengaluru .
18.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of statement of Manchaiah recorded in the hospital .
Ex.P.3 is the copy of the sketch of the place of accident.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of spot mahazar.
Ex.P.7 is the Motor Vehicle Accident Report.
Ex.P.8 is the copy of wound certificate in which reason for the injuries suffered by Manchaiah is noted as RTA on 18.08.2023 .

19. Ex.P.9 is the copy of chargesheet filed by Banashankari Traffic police in crime No.442/2023 against Jerry Abraham , S/o. Suresh Babu, rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JD-2490 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279, 338 of IPC, 134 (a&b) , 187 of IMV Act.

Discharge summary shows that since 18.08.2023 to 02.09.2023 Manchaiah was inpatient at Maharaja Agrasena hospital , Bengaluru for fracture of neck of LT femur with intertrochanteric extension with ipsilateral distal radius fracture, stricture bolbomembranous urethra, Grade - I bed sore.
Discharge summary marked at Ex.P.11 and 12 shows that since 02.09.2023 to 13.10.2023 and 15.10.2023 to 23.03.2024 Manchaiah has been treated at Dwitiya Life Care hospital, Bengaluru .
The discharge summary marked at Ex.P.25 shows that Manchaiah has been treated as an inpatient from 13.10.2023 to 15.10.2025 in Vasavi hospital , Bengaluru for Acute Ischemic stroke.

20. In this case respondents have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve the evidence placed by the petitioners regarding reason and mode of the accident, nature of the injuries suffered by Manchaiah and treatment taken by Manchaiah for the injuries suffered in the accident.

21. The evidence on record shows that on 05.09.2023 Manchaiah filed petition under Section 166 claiming compensation for the injuries suffered in the accident then during pendency of the petition in the residence on 05.04.2024 expired.

sentences.text: In this case petitioners have not produced medical evidence to show that death of Manchaiah was the consequence of the injuries suffered in the accident dated 18.08.2023.

Hence, I have concluded that on 18.08.2023 at 10.30 a.m. when manchaiah was crossing the Dr. Puneeth Raj Kumar road, Banashankari 3 rd stage, respondent No.2 Jerry Abraham , S/o. Suresh Babu,
negligently rode motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JD-2490 on the wrong lane dashed the same to the back of Manchaiah , thereby caused the accident, caused grievous injuries to Manchaiah. Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative and Addl. Issue in the negative.
23. Issue No.2:

In the evidence affidavit PW1 stated that in the accident Manchaiah suffered grievous injuries to left leg and left hand , took treatment at Maharaja Agrasena hospital , Bengaluru as an inpatient from 18.08.2023 to 02.09.2023 then shifted to Dwitiya Life Care hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein taken treatment as an inpatient from 02.09.2023 to 13.10.2023 and from 15.10.2023 to 23.03.2024.
PW1 stated that he has spent Rs.30,00,000/- towards hospital , medical charges, funeral and other ceremonies etc.
24. In the written statements respondents No.1 and 2 denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by Manchaiah.
25. In the cross-examination PW1 admitted that in the residence his father Manchaiah expired and as on the date of accident his father was aged about 84 years.
PW1 admitted that his father was diabetic and denied the suggestion that his father suffered urine related problem.
PW1 denied the suggestion about fabrication of medical bills produced produced at serial No.19 in the name of Vasavi hospital to get more compensation.

26. Wound certificate, discharge summaries marked at Exs.P.10 to 12 shows that in the accident Manchaiah suffered fracture of neck of left femur with intertrochanteric extension with ipsilateral distal radius fracture, stricture Bulbomembranous Urethra, Grade I bed sore, took treatment at Maharaja Agrasena hospital , Bengaluru as an inpatient from 18.08.2023 to 02.09.2023, since from 02.09.2023 to 13.10.2023 and 15.10.2023 to 23.03.2024 Manchaiah has been cared at Dwitiya Life Care hospital, Bengaluru .
The discharge summary marked at Ex.P.25 shows that Manchaiah has been treated as an inpatient from 13.10.2023 to 15.10.2025 in Vasavi hospital, Bengaluru for Acute Ischemic stroke.

Ex.P.12 shows that Manchaiah get treated at Dwitiya Life Care hospital, Bengaluru for chronic lacunar infract, Ecentric calcific plague in the right carotid bulb, fracture of neck of left femur with intertrochanteric extension with ipsilateral distal fracture , stricture Bulbomembranous urethra, Grade-1 bed sore and other injuries.
In the medical records age of Manchaiah is noted as 85 years.
In the copy of aadhar card marked at Ex.P.13 birth year of Manchaiah is noted as 1938.

The medical bills pertaining to Maharaja Agrasena hospital , Bengaluru and Vasavi hospital, Bengaluru shows that Manchaiah has taken treatment at Maharaja Agrasena hospital , Bengaluru and Vasavi hospital by spending Rs. 3,69,861 and Rs.1,15,020/- I..e, totally Rs.4,84,861/-.
27.
Bills pertaining to Dwitiya Life Care hospital , shows that petitioners get cared Manchaiah at Dwitiya Life Care hospital by spending Rs.7,91,512/- instead of taking care in the house.

Manchaiah vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85129373/

sentences.text:
In the lengthy argument learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submitted that due to the injuries suffered in the accident Manchaiah suffered many problems including bed sore etc.,
therefore, petitioners are unable to care Manchaiah in the house, therefore, get cared at Dwitiya Life Care hospital.

29. In the lengthy argument learned Advocate appearing for the insurance company submitted that the petitioners who ought to have to cared Manchaiah, who is aged 85 years suffered from diabetic etc by keeping him in the house, therefore, they are not entitle for money spent at Dwitiya Life Care hospital, Bengaluru.

30. Considering the submission made on behalf of both the parties , age and status of Manchaiah during the period when he has been cared at Dwitiya Life Care hospital , present situation/ system of our society , I have inferred that the petitioners are entitle to receive 50% money spent to get cared Manchaiah at Dwitiya Life Care hospital, Bengaluru .

31. Considering the nature of the injuries suffered by Manchaiah , length , place and nature of treatment taken by Manchaiah for the injuries suffered in the accident, I award Rs.4,84,861/-
towards treatment charges, Rs.3,300/- towards ambulance, conveyance charges, Rs.3,94,106/-
towards money spent for Dwitiya Life Care hospital (50% only) and Rs.30,000/- towards attendance and conveyance charges during treatment period at Maharaja Agrasena hospital ,
Bengaluru and Vasavi hospital, Bengaluru.

32. Hence, I came to the conclusion that the present petitioners, children of Manchaiah are entitle to receive Rs.9,12,267/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from 05.04.2024 as compensation from the respondents.
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs 1.
Treatment charges 4,84,861-00 2. Ambulance, conveyance 3,300-00 charges 3. Money spent towards 3,94,106-00 Dwitiya Life Care hospital (50%)
4. Attendant, conveyance 30,000-00 charges Total 9,12,267-00
Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly.
33.Issue No.3:
In the written statement respondent No.1 insurance company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JD- 2490 as on the date of incident.
In para No.11 of the written statement , respondent No.2 noted the identification number of the policy under which motorcycle had insurance coverage as on the date of incident.
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on the date of incident , respondent No.2 owner/rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JD-2490 has violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that respondents being the insurer and owner of the motorcycle bearing Manchaiah vs Liberty General Insurance Co. Ltd on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85129373/
6 No.KA-02-JD-2490 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.3 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER

The petition dated 05.09.2023 filed by petitioner Manchaiah under Section 166 of IMV Act and after death of petitioner Manchaiah, continued by his children are hereby partly allowed in the following terms:

The respondents being the insurer and owner of motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JD-2490 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.9,12,267/- (Rupees Nine lakhs twelve thousand two hundred and sixty seven only ) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from 05.04.2024 to the petitioners as compensation.
The respondent No.1, being the Insurer of motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JD-2490 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to petitioners by crediting the same to the bank account of petitioner No.1(a) Shivaramu (PW1) .
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.

(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 6th day of May , 2025)
(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
